speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I am here to evaluate the skin condition on your left dorsal hand. To begin, can you describe the onset and duration of these symptoms, and have you noticed any changes in size, color, or texture?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing that history. Given your age and history of sun exposure, I need to focus on the specific appearance of the lesion on your left dorsal hand. Can you describe the shape, color, and whether it has raised borders or a central area of clearing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. The clinical presentation of a rough, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand of a sun-exposed individual is classic for this condition; the previous mention of a urinary tract infection was likely an error or unrelated finding.
